clue.text: Head of college has no peace to study

parts.note: the absence of peace is war
a den is a private study or work room

explanation.surface: A college head is told there is no peaceful place to read.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden is the title of the head at several Oxford and Cambridge colleges.

clue.text: Vote for new candidate Conservatives pronounced trendy

indicators.note: pronounced means the word for conservatives is said aloud, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: the political right means conservatives
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Conservatives declare a new candidate fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' turns RIGHT into its sound-alike WRITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A write-in is a vote cast by writing in a name not printed on the ballot.

clue.text: Like something from the past some reporters turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards
some means only part of the word reporters is used

explanation.surface: Some journalists arrive looking old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ORTER from inside REPORTERS and 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro means imitating or evoking styles of the past.

clue.text: Selectively provided seats for some who were standing

definitions.text: Selectively provided seats for some who were standing

parts.words: Selectively provided seats for some who were standing
parts.note: candidates stand for parliament, and voters choose which of them gets a seat

explanation.surface: Seats handed out to only some of those standing up.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is of standing passengers being offered seats; the standing is as candidates at an election.
explanation.definitionFit: Those chosen by voters to take seats in parliament are voted in.

clue.text: Special spread provided for worker in digs

indicators.note: special letters are treated out of the ordinary, so the next word is rearranged here

explanation.surface: A special spread of food is laid on for an archaeologist at the dig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' signals that SPREAD is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A spader is one who digs with a spade, a labourer working the ground.

clue.text: American who wrote essay and verse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
an essay is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: An American author produced essays as well as verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is metrical writing, the same thing as poems collectively.

clue.text: Damage part of watch around edge

indicators.note: around means the watch part encloses the edge word

parts.note: a detent is a catch in a watch or clock mechanism
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A watch has damage to a part around its edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' suggests a timepiece being damaged; a detent is the small catch in its mechanism, and 'around' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment means harm or damage.

clue.text: Jet-setters taxi to and from these areas

definitions.text: Jet-setters taxi to and from these areas

parts.words: Jet-setters taxi to and from these areas
parts.note: jets themselves taxi along airport strips before take-off and after landing

explanation.surface: Wealthy travellers take cabs to and from certain districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet-setters' reads as rich travellers and 'taxi' as cabs; really the jets taxi on airfield strips.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the airfield strips where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: He and I, for example, have very different values for these

definitions.text: He and I, for example, have very different values for these

parts.words: He and I, for example, have very different values for these
parts.note: He and I are chemical symbols for helium and iodine, whose atoms differ greatly in mass

explanation.surface: Two people who disagree deeply about values.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He and I' look like two people; they are chemical symbols for helium and iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the relative masses of atoms of elements such as helium and iodine.

clue.text: Deposit second pound in it

indicators.note: in means the pound letter is placed inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for pound (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Instructions to put a second pound coin into a slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Silt is fine sediment that a river leaves behind as a deposit.

clue.text: Legally enforcing forfeit of ring, estate being redistributed

indicators.note: redistributing shares things out afresh, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A court seizes a ring and shares out an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being redistributed' rearranges RING and ESTATE together; 'of' and the comma are link material.
explanation.definitionFit: To estreat is a legal term for extracting a forfeited fine or recognisance for enforcement.

clue.text: Answer to be found in chemistry lab

definitions.text: to be found in chemistry lab
definitions.meaning: a glass vessel with a bent-down neck used for distilling

explanation.surface: Where to look for the solution: the chemistry lab.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a witty reply and a long-necked distillation flask.

clue.text: Man involved with a girl on the side

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled together and reordered

explanation.surface: A man having an affair with a girl on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles MAN and A GIRL; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginal means at the edge or margin, so on the side.

clue.text: Start during peacetime, with party getting back in

parts.note: in can mean during, as in 'in wartime'

indicators.note: in means the reversed party goes inside the truce

parts.note: a truce is a period of peace

indicators.note: getting back means the word for party is read backwards

parts.note: do is informal for a party

explanation.surface: A party resumes during a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting back' reverses the party word and 'in' signals the container; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce something is to start or initiate it.

clue.text: User's very confused, takes another view

indicators.note: confused means the letters are muddled up

parts.note: the word with its s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A very confused user looks at things again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges USERS and VERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurveys means examines or inspects again, taking a fresh view.

clue.text: Favourites getting walkover?

indicators.note: over means the word for walk is turned round

parts.note: a step is a single pace of walking

explanation.surface: Favourites in a race enjoying an easy walkover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walkover' splits into 'walk' and 'over': STEP reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pets are favourites, as in teacher's pets.

clue.text: Sauce unfinished? Bother!

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the sauce is dropped

parts.note: pesto is an Italian basil sauce

explanation.surface: A cook exclaims in frustration that the sauce is not finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the final O of PESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is a nuisance, something that bothers you; the noun stands for the exclamation.

clue.text: Beer concealed by pupils, nervously

indicators.note: concealed by means the answer is tucked away inside these words

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren nervously hiding a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed by' points to the letters running across PUPILS and NERVOUSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilsner is a pale lager beer originating in Pilsen.

clue.text: Making less trouble about limited edition

indicators.note: about means the trouble word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a ruction is a noisy disturbance or row
ED is the shortened, limited form of edition

explanation.surface: A fuss over a limited-edition print run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'limited' shows edition is cut down to its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction is the act of making something smaller or less.

clue.text: Revolted pure converts with sin

indicators.note: converts means changes form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pure soul is converted to sin and turns rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' rearranges PURE and SIN; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprisen means having risen up in revolt, revolted.

clue.text: Watched attentively as a wicket falls after spells of bowling

indicators.note: falls after means these pieces come after the spells of bowling

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire keeps a close eye as a wicket falls after several overs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a spell of six deliveries; W is a wicket on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee something is to supervise or watch over it.

clue.text: Penetrate, with rook being taken by knight, say

indicators.note: being taken by means the rook goes inside the word for knight

parts.note: a knight is an example of a chess piece
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess move where a knight captures a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knight, say' is a chess piece; R for rook goes inside PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to puncture or penetrate.

clue.text: Almost everyone preparing to fight — that's scary

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word for everyone is lost

parts.note: all means everyone
arming is taking up weapons in readiness for battle

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone getting ready for war is a frightening sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarming describes something frightening or disturbing.

clue.text: Unpleasant type of animal seen by river

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
an otter is a river-dwelling animal

explanation.surface: An unpleasant creature spotted beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter is an old-fashioned word for a cad or nasty person.

clue.text: Rebel said what?

parts.note: the leader of the 1381 Peasants' Revolt had a first name that sounds like the question word

explanation.surface: A rebel asks someone to repeat themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381; his first name sounds like the question word.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Wat, the famous English peasant rebel leader.

clue.text: Accommodates unappreciative types outside central hotels

indicators.note: outside means the ungrateful people surround the central letters

parts.note: ingrates are ungrateful people

indicators.note: central means the middle letters of the word hotels are taken

explanation.surface: A town houses ungrateful people around its central hotels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' takes the middle two letters of HOTELS, and 'outside' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to take in or incorporate, so accommodating something.

clue.text: Recognise architectural distinction in catalogue

definitions.meaning: in Britain a building of special architectural interest is officially designated or protected

explanation.surface: A notable building is recorded in a register.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, a 'listed' building is one officially protected for its architectural or historic importance.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to designate a building as protected; the noun means an itemised register.

clue.text: Uttered harsh statements as artist put foot down

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
putting your foot down on the accelerator means you sped

explanation.surface: A painter swears harshly while slamming on the accelerator.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasped means spoke in a grating, harsh voice.

clue.text: The saint of those who drive?

definitions.text: The saint of those who drive?

parts.words: The saint of those who drive?
parts.note: drivers here are golfers, and the patron saint of Scotland is linked with St ..., the home of golf

explanation.surface: Asking which patron saint protects motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' suggests motorists; it is a golf shot, and St Andrews in Scotland is golf's home.
explanation.definitionFit: The patron saint of Scotland gives his name to the town that is golf's spiritual home.
